tagline: From moose country over Cameron Pass and down the Poudre.
intro: Walden sits at 8,098 feet in the middle of North Park, a bowl-shaped valley just east of the Continental Divide. Highway 14 runs southeast through Gould along the Michigan River and rises gently to Cameron Pass at 10,276 feet. The east side is another matter. The road drops steeply down Joe Wright Creek into the narrow valley of the Cache la Poudre and follows it down Poudre Canyon toward Fort Collins.

The name means hide the powder, after French trappers caught by a snowstorm in the 1820s who buried gunpowder on the riverbank. A flood in 1864 washed out Camp Collins near La Porte. The Army moved it and renamed it Fort Collins, though no fort was ever built.

moments.title: Gould
moments.text: A one-time timber town at 8,913 feet among wetlands and aspen groves, home to the Colorado State Forest headquarters and its Moose Visitor Center.

moments.title: Cameron Pass
moments.text: Named in 1870 for Robert Cameron, a former Union general, and surveyed more than once for a railroad through the Rockies, though no railroad was ever built over it.

moments.title: Rustic
moments.text: S. B. Stewart built the Rustic Hotel here on the Poudre in 1881, and it soon became a summer resort.

practical: Highway 14 is kept open year-round, but Cameron Pass takes heavy winter snow and is prone to avalanches.
